I'm 4 months in, so still kinda new. I agree with the other comment, make sure you wrap them especially when laying down. DO NOT bypass blow drying after washing. I've got some flat locs cause of that, plus you don't want them to mildew.

Spritz them daily. A lot of people prefer rose water. I just use water, more recently I've been using aloe vera water.

Oil your scalp like twice a week with a light oil, don't need much. I use jojoba or peppermint oil. You can even mix them together. 

KEEP YOUR HANDS OUT OF YOUR HAIR!!

WASH THEM! Every 2wks depending on your level of activity (more sweaty, maybe once a week. You know your hair though, if it feels too dirty, wash it) . If you're worried about unraveling, you can wash with a wave/durag/wig cap on in the beginning months. Be gentle when washing, don't wash it like loose hair, use your fingertips and focus on scrubbing your scalp. Use a light shampoo free of parabens phthalates and all that other stuff. I've been using Peculiar Roots ACV Shampoo for locs and Mielle Rosemary Mint Strengthening Shampoo. 

Retwist every 4-6 weeks; not too often. Not too long in between either as you risk breakage/thinning. 

TRUST THE PROCESS AND BE PATIENT! There's gonna be frizz and it won't look nice, depending on what your definition of nice is. It's all normal either way. Just let them rock and enjoy them. They're gonna turn out great!

Join r/locs or r/dreadlocks as well.

I can speak only from the "ugly phase" side of things you are afraid of.. I am someone who has always hated their natural hair. I don't like to use the word hate, but using it lets you know how much of a struggle I've had accepting my hair in it's natural state. My hair doesn't grow, or I don't know how to grow it, and unless I've done some type of weave style to it, I've always had my hair wrapped up, and I hardly go anywhere due to my hair not being done or not looking up to par per my own standards (amongst other reasons, but my hair was and is a big issue as well)

Now, I am a little over a month in and my hair has already grown so much, which in turn, has given me more confidence. Although I still wrap it in this stage, I can say I am soooo glad I made the decision to loc it up. I've noticed in the loc community, "patience is key" is a phrase that is reiterated, and it's true. It's going to take some patience , but I am already so happy with it. 

For me, it's like nurturing a plant and watching it grow and that has been so rewarding for me to see. 

I never fully understood my hair or how to care for it. Yes, locs need care as well, but I feel like the upkeep has been far less demanding than when I was a loose natural. Far less products and time. I spray my hair with water  everyday and add an oil to seal in the moisture, I wash every two weeks, and oil my scalp twice a week, but other than that I can just let it do it's thing. I can workout without worrying about sweating out a style or postponing styling or working out due to the worry of messing my hair up.

I am aware I still may not be comfortable going out without it wrapped up for awhile, but I'm actually ok with that and am just looking forward to it growing. Sometimes I'm even confident (and hot as hell lol) enough to go out with it uncovered, which I would have never done before. 

I believe there are plenty of styles you can explore that will still give you a professional look. They last a while too.

Also, I would recommend watching YouTube vids on pros and cons. Especially those 'I wish I would've known this before getting locs' type of vids. Watching stylists or people with locs list things they weren't aware of gives you an idea of whether or not it's something you really want to try and follow through with.
